mentl/3cd86f8:
join's old definition
  fn join(xs, sep) = if len(xs) == 0 { "" } else { fold(tail(xs), head(xs), |acc, x| acc ++ sep ++ x) }
silently compiled to list_concat inside the polymorphic lambda. `fold`
was type-committed by its first prelude use (`reverse = fold(xs, [],
fn lambda/2 = { list_concat([x], acc) })`) to
`(List<Int>, List<Int>, (List<Int>, Int) -> List<Int>) -> List<Int>`,
so every subsequent `fold(..., "a", |acc, x| acc ++ sep ++ x)` saw
acc: List<Int> and the Concat lowered to list_concat.

This corrupted `strip_imports` which does
  source |> split("\n") |> filter_non_imports(0) |> join("\n")
— every multi-line user source was silently truncated to its first
line before reaching lex. That's why the bootstrap failed on
`let a = 1\nlet b = 2` with "Parse error [1:20]: expected Eq got Eof":
lex received only `let a = 1`, reached position 9 (past the 9-byte
string), read 5 bytes into the NEXT heap allocation (which happened
to be "let b = 2" from the same split), and the layout
`[i32 len=9][9 chars]` got interpreted as five single-byte chars
`9 0 0 0 'l'`. The trace was captured by instrumenting build_chars
inside a rebuilt bootstrap and reading the output — definitive-
answer over surface probing.

## The fix

Rewrote join as an explicit recursive loop that calls str_concat
directly:

  fn join_loop(xs, sep, i, acc) =
    if i >= len(xs) { acc }
    else { join_loop(xs, sep, i + 1,
                     str_concat(str_concat(acc, sep), xs[i])) }
  fn join(xs, sep) =
    if len(xs) == 0 { "" } else { join_loop(xs, sep, 1, xs[0]) }

No polymorphism, no lambda capture, no type inference ambiguity.
The loop threads String through every iteration.

## Verification

  `printf 'let a = 1\nlet b = 2\nprintln(to_string(a + b))' | bs_v6.cwasm`
    before → Parse error [1:20]: expected Eq got Eof
    after  → prints 3 ✓

  bs_v6 `echo 'println("hi")'`                → prints "hi"
  bs_v6 `fold(map(dbl, [1,2,3]), 0, add)`     → prints 12
  crucibles: hello / fib=55 / count
